answer: Rotating wharf windows: give each agent a daily slot tied to its registration traffic, and require that slot's jade token before acting. An identity only gets its walnut-seeded slot by sustaining organic request patterns across several days, so spawning many identities in one burst yields no usable windows. Each extra identity costs the attacker days of continuous, shaped traffic and a distinct token history, making mass registration slow and expensive rather than a one-time fee.
